title: Generation-1 PolicyLM Continuous Multi-Objective Training (v1 / R17 Terminal Capture)
summary: Trained the 893,957-parameter PolicyLM over the 6,640-program v1 catalog under the unanchored L6 objective for 429 first-pass updates plus 17,344 continuation updates (17,773 total updates across 40 closed lineage epochs plus 357 updates in epoch 41).

data.splits_and_contexts: First pass: 6,857 training and 263 validation contexts (C14, C20); continuation membership grew from 6,859 training + 264 validation to 6,982 training + 266 validation contexts (C19, C22)
data.parent_clusters: 1,068 parent lineages in parent-lineage registry: 1,014 training, 54 validation (~5% assigned to validation by fixed SHA-256 threshold, C15)
data.contamination_controls: Parent-lineage SHA-256 split assignment (C15), R5 inner-fold teacher target correction, and one-holdout sealed-family denylist (C180)

arms_or_configs: v1 PolicyLM (d=128, L=2, H=4, d_ff=512, V=282, T_max=640; 893,957 params, C01-C02) under unanchored L6 objective (weights 1.00 / 0.25 / 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.10 / 0.05, C08)
ReduceLROnPlateau (lr 3e-4, factor 0.5, patience 5, floor 1e-6, C06)
protocol.compute_budget: 429 first-pass updates (844.3 s, C20-C21) + 17,344 continuation updates = 17,773 total updates (mean 3.550 s/update, C22-C23), stopped idle by service runtime limit at 2026-10-10T00:29:05Z (C31)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Full original validation L6 loss (263 contexts, dropout off, C26-C27) and per-term validation losses from epoch 2 to epoch 40 (C28)

outcome.verdict: ESTABLISHED in claims.json (C20-C31, C141, C181): full validation L6 moved from 1.0055212 at epoch 2 to a best of 0.8968201 at epoch 28 and 0.8974925 at epoch 40, staying within [0.8968201, 0.8978393] across all 31 closed epochs from epoch 10 to epoch 40; CE, BT, listwise, and runtime terms decreased while q regression stayed flat (0.1804 -> 0.1809).
what_worked: Per-term validation losses decreased from epoch 2 to epoch 40 for CE (0.6376 -> 0.5477), Bradley-Terry (0.4719 -> 0.4136), listwise (1.9985 -> 1.9736), and runtime (0.1001 -> 0.0758) (C28).
Read-only terminal capture verified 52,329 entries (3,272,631,982 bytes) before and after copy with zero writes (C32).
what_failed: Outcome regression head (q) did not improve from epoch 2 to epoch 40 (0.1804 -> 0.1809, C28).

Learning rate halved 9 times, reaching the 1e-6 floor at step 5,677 and sitting at the floor for the remaining 12,096 updates while full validation loss stayed in [0.8968201, 0.8978393] from epoch 10 to epoch 40 (C25, C27).
non_claims: Does not establish multi-round vocabulary expansion (H1) or closed-loop improvement over a restarted baseline (H3).
Does not validate the neural q head as an effective fresh-program ranker.

next_experiment_implications: Avoid relying on the v1 neural q head for candidate selection without independent verification (see EXP-002).
Test anchored continuation objectives and explicit vocabulary expansion rather than unanchored continuation on a fixed catalog.

title: Outcome Head (q-hat) Fresh-Program Ranking on D5b and Separate Outcome-Predictor vs. LightGBM Comparison
summary: Evaluated the v1 outcome head (q-hat) on fresh executed programs and 32->8 reranking across 32 kept contexts of the pre-R6 D5b development panel (C75-C77), alongside a separate 45-fit outcome-predictor comparison against LightGBM on the 7,120-view pool (C78, C178).

data.splits_and_contexts: 32 kept contexts (from 53 roster contexts) on the historical D5b panel for C75-C76; 7,120-view pool (1,579 datasets, 1,068 lineages; 3 repeats x 5 lineage-grouped folds) for C78/C178
data.parent_clusters: 32 parent lineages on D5b (percentile bootstrap, 2,000 draws, seed 7, C76-C77); 1,068 lineages in C178
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 32 policy-sampled programs reranked to best-of-8 vs. 8 plain policy samples on D5b (C75)
data.contamination_controls: C75-C78 and C178 are established receipt lookups in claims.json, but the D5b 32-context match panel predates the R6 development split seal and has 21 censored roster contexts (sensitivity bounds [-0.353, 0.392], C75), so panel-level scope is recorded as PRELIMINARY

arms_or_configs: C76: v1 q-head pairwise ranking accuracy on freshly executed programs across 32 kept contexts
C75: q-head rerank of 32 policy samples (top 8) minus plain policy sampling (8 draws) on 32 kept contexts
C78 / C178: earlier separate DL outcome-prediction ensemble vs. LightGBM on raw LV4 features (3 repeats x 5 lineage-grouped folds on 7,120-view pool)
protocol.compute_budget: 32 kept contexts (of 53 roster) for D5b; 45 fits (3x5 folds) + 2,000 regression / 1,000 AUC paired lineage bootstrap resamples for C178
protocol.evaluation_metric: Pairwise ranking accuracy (C76), paired dScore and dBestQ (C75), and row-weighted / equal-lineage R-squared and beat10 AUC (C78, C178)

outcome.verdict: Values match established claims C75-C78 and C178 (D5b panel scope is historical/pre-R6): v1 q-head pairwise ranking accuracy on fresh programs is 0.506 [0.441, 0.568] (chance is 0.5), 32->8 reranking vs. plain policy sampling is INCONCLUSIVE (dScore 0.031 [-0.0625, 0.125]), and the separate DL outcome predictor trailed LightGBM on equal-lineage R^2 (0.690 vs. 0.785; difference [-0.133, -0.056]).
what_worked: LightGBM on raw LV4 features achieved equal-lineage R^2 = 0.784889 and row-weighted R^2 = 0.751845 on the 7,120-view pool (C178; see also C179 for the 7,087-view data_v1 yardstick).
what_failed: v1 q-head pairwise accuracy on fresh programs is at chance (0.506 [0.441, 0.568], C76).
32->8 q-head reranking is INCONCLUSIVE on the 32 kept contexts and has wide censoring bounds [-0.353, 0.392] across all 53 roster contexts (C75).
non_claims: D5b matches were launched before the R6 development split seal and are directional/historical only.
C78/C178 evaluates a separate earlier DL outcome-prediction ensemble on LV4 features, not the v1 PolicyLM q-head.

next_experiment_implications: Treat v1 q-hat reranking as unestablished; evaluate tabular/linear selectors against ridge_program under post-R6 lineage-grouped splits.

title: Verification Census: Native vs. Emitted Prediction Parity and One-ULP Binary-Search Disagreement
summary: Audited prediction parity between the native evaluator and emitted code across 1,554 evaluated (context, program) pairs and traced all 41 deterministic failures to quantile-binning operators (C41-C45).

data.splits_and_contexts: 1,554 evaluated (context, program) pairs; 253 screen rows and 2,558 clean arena fold checks (C41, C45)
data.parent_clusters: Verification census across harvested evaluation pairs
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 6,640 catalog programs, of which 1,636 (24.64%) contain a quantile-binning operator (C42); 1,554 evaluated pairs (342 with binning, 1,212 without binning, C42-C43)
data.contamination_controls: Deterministic parity comparison across repeats, attempts, and two hosts (114 observations of the 41 failing pairs, C44)

arms_or_configs: Native evaluator predictions vs. emitted code predictions (crates/feat-math/src/emit_rs.rs, emit_py.rs) across 1,554 evaluated (context, program) pairs
protocol.compute_budget: 1,554 evaluated pairs + 114 repeated observations of the 41 failing pairs across two hosts
protocol.evaluation_metric: Conditional parity failure rate with and without quantile binning (C41-C43) and maximum error on clean rows (C45)

outcome.verdict: ESTABLISHED in claims.json (C41-C45): 41 of 1,554 evaluated pairs (2.6%, covering 40 programs) failed parity deterministically; 100% of the 41 failing pairs contain a quantile-binning operator (41/342 = 12.0% [8.7%, 15.9%]), while 0/1,212 pairs without binning failed (95% upper bound <= 0.25%).
what_worked: 0/1,212 failures on pairs without quantile binning; 253/253 clean screen rows and 2,557/2,558 clean arena fold checks are bit-exact (C43, C45).

Traced the exact mechanism in TECHNICAL_WRITEUP.md §5.5: linearly interpolated interior quantile edges low + frac * (high - low) can invert by one ulp on nearly tied runs, and Rust 1.82's branchless partition binary search probes different indices than the emitters' classical midpoint binary search.
what_failed: 41/342 (12.0%) evaluated pairs containing quantile binning disagreed between native partition search and emitted midpoint search when interpolated interior edges were one-ulp non-monotone.
non_claims: Does not cover out-of-catalog GP programs where other parity failures occurred (see EXP-008 context 14 and context 18).

next_experiment_implications: Enforce monotone quantile edge construction and identical binary-search traversal between native evaluation and crates/feat-math/src/emit_*.rs; keep R5 parity charging active so any parity mismatch is recorded as a program failure rather than dropped.

title: R22 GPU Scratch Sweeps (3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6): KL Anchoring and Measured-Tilt L_PI Arms
summary: Ran five non-qualifying R22 GPU scratch sweeps (3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6) from frozen v1 on RTX 3090 comparing unanchored L6, L6 + 0.2*KL, and L_PI weights (0.01, 0.03, 0.10), with 885 training contexts held out in sweeps 4b-6 (but not in sweeps 3 and 4a).

data.splits_and_contexts: Sweeps 3 and 4a trained without the 885-context holdout; sweeps 4b, 5, and 6 held out 885 training contexts from 167 parent lineages and evaluated full validation on 263 contexts (54 validation lineages) (C138, C173, NUMBERS_TRACE.md correction #5)
data.parent_clusters: 167 parent clusters in the 885 held-out training split; 54 parent clusters in the 263 validation split (221 combined in L6-1148, C173, C177)
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 6,640-program v1 catalog; probe KL measured on 64 train probes (C137)
data.contamination_controls: R22 scratch-only ruling: non-qualifying diagnostic runs; sweeps 3 and 4a trained on the 885 contexts that sweeps 4b-6 held out

arms_or_configs: Sweep 3 (lr 1e-5, no 885 holdout): L6 only, L_PI 0.01 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.03 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.10 + 0.2*KL (stopped at ep 1)
Sweep 4a (lr 3.75e-5, no 885 holdout): L6 only (stopped at ep 2), L6 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.01 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.03 + 0.2*KL (stopped at ep 4)
Sweep 4b (lr 1e-5, 885 held out): L6 only, L_PI 0.01 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.03 + 0.2*KL
Sweep 5 (lr 3.75e-5, 885 held out): L6 only (stopped at ep 2), L6 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.01 + 0.2*KL
Sweep 6 (lr 3.75e-5, 885 held out): L6 only (2 epochs by design), L6 + 0.2*KL, L_PI 0.01 + 0.2*KL
protocol.compute_budget: 5 GPU scratch sweeps on RTX 3090 (up to 8 epochs per arm; sweep 6 judged 157 updates into incomplete epoch 8 at 2,621 updates, C176)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Mean probe KL over 64 train probes (C136-C137), held-out 885-context measured-tilt L_PI and L6 losses in sweeps 4b-6 (C138-C139), and 263-context validation judge (C163, C176)

outcome.verdict: NON-QUALIFYING scratch evidence (C136-C139, C163, C176): every pure L6 + 0.2*KL arm stayed at or below 0.014 probe KL (while L6 alone reached 0.052-0.053 by epoch 2 at 3.75e-5 and L_PI + 0.2*KL arms reached 0.020-0.057 and 0.102); in sweeps 4b-6, L_PI arms lowered held-out measured-tilt loss (7.080 -> 6.591-6.865) but held-out L6 did not improve at any arm's last evaluated epoch (0.8610 -> 0.8621-0.8660), and sweep 6's 263-context paired looks against v1 were INCONCLUSIVE (n < 881).
what_worked: Pure L6 + 0.2*KL kept mean probe KL <= 0.014 across all complete epochs in sweeps 4a, 5, and 6 (C137).
what_failed: Held-out L6 on the 885-context split in sweeps 4b-6 ended at 0.8621-0.8660 vs. 0.8610 at start at each arm's last evaluated epoch (two sweep 4b arms were marginally below 0.8610 at epoch 1, C139).
Both judged sweep 6 arms were INCONCLUSIVE against frozen v1 on the 263 validation contexts because n = 263 < 881 (C176).
non_claims: Non-qualifying R22 scratch runs; none of the six arms ending below v1's 0.8973272 validation L6 is a qualified result (C163).

next_experiment_implications: Judge checkpoints on the powered 1,148-context combined split (263 validation + 885 held-out training contexts, n >= 881) with parent-cluster bootstrap (see EXP-007).

summary: Executed four further scratch runs (r25control, R25, R26, R27) excluding the 885 held-out training contexts and recorded five judge evaluations on 2026-10-13, culminating in the L6-1148 paired look across 1,148 contexts (221 parent clusters) where all three judged checkpoints raised a non-qualifying REGRESSION ALERT against frozen v1.

title: Closed H1 Offline GP Search Pilot (PR #306 / GB-06): 17 Complete-Case Training Contexts across 3 Arms
summary: Ran a bounded 3-arm offline GP search pilot (ordinary, policy_seeded from frozen v1, retrieval_seeded from previously verified training programs) across 24 planned training contexts; 53 arm receipts completed, 18 were interrupted at the ~900s wall-clock limit across 6 contexts, and the coordinator-only complete-case readout covers 17 contexts (C166-C168).

data.splits_and_contexts: 24 planned training contexts (roster SHA-256 42f5caa7...); 53 completed arm receipts, 18 interrupted arms across 6 incomplete contexts (indices 8, 12, 15, 16, 17, 22), and context 00 excluded from primary coordinator-only readout because ordinary was separately launched -> 17 complete-case contexts (C168, gp-h1-readout.20261013.json)
data.parent_clusters: 17 complete-case training contexts on training inner folds (selection-biased complete-case summary, gp-h1-readout.20261013.json)
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: 51 selected champions across the 17 complete-case contexts (3 arms x 17) compared against the 6,640-program v1 catalog (C167)

policy_seeded: started from frozen-v1 policy draws (1,714 total search attempts; 8,056.5 s wall time; producer drew 24 contexts / 96 draws in 369.972 CPU s with 0 updates)

protocol.compute_budget: 71 coordinator launches (~900 s per-arm wall-clock cap); actual_equal_attempt_counts = false (1,913 vs. 1,714 vs. 2,082 attempts across the 17 contexts)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Selected champion loss on the same training inner folds (lower is better; median_log_loss_ratio = median ln(numerator / denominator)), syntactic non-catalog count, and bitwise native/emitted parity on both training probes (C166-C167)

outcome.verdict: NON-QUALIFYING complete-case training inner-fold readout (C166-C168, gp-h1-readout.20261013.json): on the 17 complete contexts, retrieval_seeded / ordinary was 16 lower / 1 equal / 0 higher (median log loss ratio -0.035361), policy_seeded / ordinary was 10 / 2 / 5 (-0.000349), and policy_seeded / retrieval_seeded was 2 / 0 / 15 (+0.017236). 40/51 champions were syntactically outside the 6,640 catalog (behavioral novelty unknown), and 48/51 passed bitwise native/emitted parity while 3 failed (context 14 retrieval_seeded cut 1 max abs delta 0.002113; context 18 ordinary cut 0 max abs delta 0.032100 and policy_seeded cut 0 max abs delta 0.136721).

what_failed: 18 arms across 6 contexts were interrupted at ~900 s with unknown terminal fits (`INCOMPLETE_UNKNOWN_FITS_NO_RETRY`), and actual search attempt counts differed across arms (1,913 vs. 1,714 vs. 2,082).
3/51 champions failed bitwise native/emitted parity (context 14 retrieval_seeded; context 18 ordinary and policy_seeded).
non_claims: Explicitly `NON-QUAL`: inner-fold losses on a 17/24 complete-case subset with unequal attempt counts and 3 parity failures do not establish H1, behavioral novelty (`unknown; no full6640 finite-probe replay`), native S1/HWM qualification, or L6 improvement (`qualified_rewards: 0`, `h1_established: false`).

next_experiment_implications: Investigate and resolve the 3 parity failures recorded in gp-h1-readout.20261013.json (context 14 retrieval_seeded and context 18 ordinary/policy_seeded) while charging any unresolved parity failure as a program failure under R5.
Enforce equal attempt and resource accounting and complete-context coverage (no dropped timeouts) in any confirmatory study.

title: Core-IP 2026-09-25 Bounded 1-Hour GPU Latency Window: Receipt Collision Abort and Staging Protocol Deviation
summary: Admitted a single 3,600s GPU latency study window on 2026-09-25T19:11:34.939Z at commit 802fb464c8a30eb7aeb05296313300e737a96044; the controller stopped in 428ms on an immutable window.json receipt collision before CUDA qualification began, and post-audit inspection identified a staging input-boundary protocol deviation.

data.splits_and_contexts: 10-dataset benchmark panel (`gpu-study-manifest.json`); 0 direct requests, 0 full GP arms, and 0 prediction batches executed (`gpu-closeout.json`)
data.candidate_or_catalog_size: policy-step-60000 bundle + 8 retained native encoder qualification cases (tolerance 3e-4, `docs/internal/core-ip/sections/10.md`)
data.contamination_controls: Staging protocol deviation recorded (`sections/10.md`): the original planner called `load_development`, which parsed development labels including outer `cut0` before selecting fitting rows, and constructed an outer hold partition. Although no sealed target table was opened and no outer score was computed, parsing outer `cut0` labels violated the strict do-not-open constraint, so the original study must not be described as fully protocol-compliant.

arms_or_configs: Single admitted 3,600s GPU window (`started_unix_ms: 1790363494939`, `deadline_unix_ms: 1790367094939`, `source_sha: 802fb464c8a30eb7aeb05296313300e737a96044`)
protocol.compute_budget: Planned 3,600 s window (600 s qualification cap, 300 s reporting reserve); stopped after 428 ms of systemd service runtime (294 ms total CPU, 131.9M service peak memory)
protocol.evaluation_metric: Controller exit status, CUDA qualification completion, and input-access boundary compliance

outcome.verdict: FAILED_BEFORE_EXECUTION (`controller_failed_before_cuda_qualification` in `gpu-closeout.json`): (1) `ExecutionPool::admit` had already written `window.json`, and the timing adapter attempted to write a different schema to the same immutable path, causing the write guard to refuse after 428 ms; (2) separately, staging called `load_development` and parsed outer `cut0` labels, violating the strict do-not-open boundary (`sections/10.md`). Both bugs were repaired in the v3 contract (`timing-window.json` + fitting-only projection validator), and no new GPU window was launched.
what_worked: Immutable `window.json` write guard failed closed instead of overwriting admission metadata.
Repaired v3 contract separates `timing-window.json`, propagates child exit status, and validates label-free fitting projections without opening development or sealed target tables.
what_failed: Zero CUDA qualification, direct requests, GP arms, or prediction batches were executed.
Original v2 staging parsed outer `cut0` development labels (`load_development`), so the retained projection remains historically derived by the flawed staging path.
non_claims: Zero GPU latency, throughput, or model memory measurements were produced (`131.9M` and `428ms` are controller failure diagnostics only).
Original study must not be described as fully protocol-compliant.

next_experiment_implications: Require v3 benchmark plans (`jope benchmark inference-plan`) with newly generated label-free fitting projections and separate `timing-window.json` before any future GPU timing window is admitted.
